plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. This holds regardless of other bidders' beliefs about my strategy, since my payment doesn't depend on my own bid amount when I win. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and the price you pay never depends on your own bid except in determining whether you win. Overbidding risks paying more than your value; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds regardless of what others do, I will bid exactly my value of $34.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - you win exactly when your value exceeds theirs, and you pay their bid (not yours), so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $45.
